newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns listed firms over false information.
newsitem.headline: China warns listed firms over false information.

text.p: China's securities authorities on Friday warned listed firms that any company found including false information in annual reports would be harshly punished.
The Chins Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) said in a circular that several instances of false information, including incorrect figures, were cound in some of the 1996 annual reports issued.

"This must be carefully monitored by local securities authorities, exchanges and listed firms," it said. "The accuracy of the results issued by listed firms and standardisation of information release are the keys to the healthy development of the securities markets."

All Chinese firms listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges are required by exchange rules to post their 1996 annual results before April 30. About 100 of the more than 500 firms have so far done so.

The CSRC did not name any violators but trading in the shares in one firm, Shenzhen-listed Hainan Minyuan Modern Agricultural Development Co, has been suspended since March 1 due to alleged violations of accounting rules.

The CSRC ordered local securities authorities and exchanges to immediately organise a thorough probe into the 1996 annual results already issued and report to the central authorities if they found any problems.

"Serious investigations must be conducted in those firms found to have posted extraordinary turnover increases in non-essential businesses and have planned unusual high returns," the CRSC said in the circular, published in the official media.
"Price movements of these companies must be closely monitored," it added.
"Anyone found to have taken advantage of the annual results reporting season to do insider trading, rig prices or engage in other irregularities must be punished immediately," it said.
All listed firms were required to do an immediate check and report any problems to the securities authorities, the circular said.
Officials in those companies found to have included false and misleading information would be harshly punished, it said, but gave no details.
Lawyers and accountants found to collaborate with listed firms to make false statements would be prosecuted, it said.

Minyuan, a Hainan-based producer of agricultural and aquatic products which has diversified into property, tourism and telecommunications, said in its 1996 annual report that it had chalked up a 1996 net profit of 485.29 million yuan against the previous year's 375,704 yuan.
